scene.kind: observed HST/WFC3 UVIS F814W morphology of the central region of NGC 1705, reprojected at angular scale factor 1.0
scene.object: NGC 1705 (central region around the super star cluster NGC 1705-1)

product.name: hlsp_legus_hst_uvis_ngc1705_f814w_v1_drc.fits
product.collection: LEGUS (Legacy ExtraGalactic UV Survey) high-level science product, MAST
product.units: electrons per second per output pixel (BUNIT ELECTRONS/S)
product.weight_map: not distributed with the public mosaic (the header names f814w_exp_drc_wht.fits, which is not part of the product)

scene.credit: NGC 1705 F814W: HST/WFC3 UVIS, programme GO-13364 (LEGUS, PI D. Calzetti); high-level science product hlsp_legus_hst_uvis_ngc1705_f814w_v1 from MAST.
scene.band_policy: F814W morphology used as a fixed relative-intensity template with the monochromatic 1.65 um PSFs; no colour, spectral conversion or H-band prediction

centre.method: flux-weighted centroid within 6 px of the brightest pixel within 15 arcsec of the target position (NGC 1705-1)

wcs.handedness: north up, east left (+x west, +y north); determinant of CD negative
wcs.distortion: removed by drizzle (TAN WCS without SIP or lookup tables)
wcs.local_north_note: the template axes follow the projection plane; at the template centre local north is rotated by this angle from +y (meridian convergence), and the local scale differs from the plane scale by the recorded amount

target.orientation: +x west, +y north; displayed north up, east left. The simulated PSFs have no sky orientation of their own; this mapping is a presentation choice.

resampling.method: exact separable pixel-area integration: each output cell sums every input pixel's count rate times the fraction of its area inside the cell (flux conserving; equivalent to a square kernel of one input pixel)
resampling.added_response: one output-cell box of the target step (R); the input's own pixel and drizzle response is part of the observed image and is not added again

sky.pipeline: the drizzled mosaic is sky-subtracted by the pipeline (per-exposure MDRIZSKY recorded in the header table)
sky.residual_estimate: 3-sigma-clipped median of covered pixels at r >= 120 arcsec from the centre
sky.reason: the galaxy envelope still declines at that radius, so the level is an upper bound on residual sky rather than sky alone

quality.method: nearest exposure pixel at each cutout pixel centre through the aligned FLC WCS (with its distortion); this approximates, but is not, each exposure pixel's drizzle footprint

saturated_core.definition: cutout pixels whose nearest exposure pixel is saturation-flagged in every covering exposure, without dilation: an approximate extent of the saturated core of NGC 1705-1, not an exact one

conservative_envelope.definition: each exposure's saturation flags dilated by one mosaic pixel, then intersected across exposures: a deliberately enlarged region that contains the flagged core and unsaturated neighbours; it is the region marked on the page

quality.flux_note: the delivered flux inside either region is limited by saturation and depends on the approximate region definition; it is neither the core's true flux nor a bound on it, and the true core flux is not recoverable from these data

conservative_counts.definition: with saturation and cosmic-ray flags dilated by one mosaic pixel (an upper estimate)

quality.treatment: no repair, fill, clipping or masking: the delivered values are kept and the saturated core is disclosed; its peak and flux are not faithful and no detail is invented
quality.membership: no object was masked and all observed structure is retained; membership in NGC 1705 was not determined for individual sources, so unrelated foreground stars or background galaxies cannot be excluded from this single band

normalization.rule: unit total over the full template cutout

noise.policy: residual observational noise retained; no denoising, smoothing or new noise draws

observational_psf.policy: the template keeps Hubble's effective F814W image response (optics, detector, drizzle with gaussian kernel, pixfrac 0.9); it is not removed, modelled or matched
observational_psf.model: not quantified as a PSF model

indicative_resolution.method: isolated local maxima 3-60 e-/s, 25-60 arcsec from the centre, no neighbour above 20 % of the peak within 12 px; FWHM = 2.355 x the background-subtracted second-moment radius within 4 px
indicative_resolution.caveat: a crude, estimator-dependent indication of the mosaic's effective resolution (truncated moments of faint sources, some possibly compact clusters); not a measured PSF

window.orientation: north up, east left (+x west, +y north on the template's projection plane)

saturation_envelope_box_cells.definition: template cells touching the conservative saturation envelope (flags dilated by one mosaic pixel); an enlarged marker, not the exact saturated extent

window.note: the observation crop is declared separately from the PSF panels' 64 x 64 crop; the native window (156 cells, about 8.7 arcsec) is recorded in the flux accounting and the template extends to 312 cells for convolution context

display.raster: row 0 of the PNG is the north (+y) edge; columns increase towards the west (+x)

references.citation: Leschinski, K. et al. (2016), SimCADO - an instrument data simulator package for MICADO at the E-ELT, section 3.4 and Figure 3
references.used_for: the fixed source -> optical PSF -> observed image method

references.citation: Simioni, M. et al. (2026), The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: simulated observations of star forming clumps at cosmic noon, MNRAS 552, stag1714, section 5.2 and Figure 5
references.used_for: using an observed HST/LEGUS image of NGC 1705 as a source template (their three-copy arrangement and assumed redshift are not reproduced)

reference_note: Method only: no MICADO/ELT angular resolution, exposure, sensitivity or performance assumption is transferred to this 2 m simulation.
